description:
KCB's remaining counts and KMI's Steps 8–10 — the two specs the ladder ranks last, taken together because KMI's second count IS KCB's re-run.

KCB, per docs/reference/promotability.md: 'the most work, and the most implemented.' FIVE independent counts as of 0.5.0 with NO fold outstanding — V-1…V-7 landed at 0.5.0, MA-6/MA-8/MA-9 at 0.4.9. What remains is four re-runs of folded text plus a re-run outstanding since 2026-07-22: `e2e-media-transform.md` (the 0.3.0 AgentCard-extension shape), `e2e-live-schema-mutation.md` (V-2/V-4/V-5/V-7 blocking, now against the 0.5.0 fold), `kcb-subscription-firehose.md` (§4.2 backpressure, KCB 0.4.7) and `kcb-cross-owner-posture.md` (§4.3 autonomy posture, KCB 0.4.8). `89` clears the fifth (Steps 5–7 of the multi-authority walk), which is why this depends on it.

READING GREEN IS THE NAMED HAZARD HERE. 'KCB is the spec where reading `green` as a verdict does the most damage: `kcs:live-schema-mutation` and `kcs:multi-authority` both came back green over passes with four and six blocking deltas open (DR-7, DR-8).' Walk the prose.

WHAT WILL STILL BLOCK KCB AFTER FOUR CLEAN RE-RUNS, and must be stated rather than discovered later: §4.2 and §4.3 lack a KCS encoding entirely (DR-12, DR-13); count (ii)'s encoding exists but must be EXTENDED past the fold it predates (DR-7); §4.3 carries ADR-0013's retained second-independent-implementation condition (W3); and ADR-0014 — the single finding of the fold cross-read — lands with counts (ii) and (iii), moving neither and closing neither. The reference implementation read against the folded text shows the standalone manifest 0.5.0 removed is still its only crawl path (AG-1) and its manifest type carries neither `version` nor `schema_id` (AG-2), so §7 is unexercised outside this tree.

KMI: 'the fold landed; now a re-run, then a wait.' MA-5's two optional §2 fields and MA-10's answerable absence went in additively at 0.3.5. What is left on count (i) is a re-run of Steps 8–10; after that KMI is blocked on KCB's re-run, which is not KMI's work.

userStories.title: The four KCB re-runs, walked against folded text, one verdict each
acceptanceCriteria: `e2e-media-transform.md`, `e2e-live-schema-mutation.md`, `kcb-subscription-firehose.md` and `kcb-cross-owner-posture.md` are each re-run against the current folded text, each with its own recorded verdict against the section it gates. Five counts 'each gating only its own section' — a combined verdict destroys that structure.
The walks are against the PROSE. DR-7 and DR-8 record two of these very encodings returning green over passes with four and six blocking deltas open, so an encoding's exit code is not the verdict.
`e2e-live-schema-mutation.md`'s V-2/V-4/V-5/V-7 are individually re-checked against the 0.5.0 fold that landed 2026-08-26, since that fold is what the re-run exists to test.

userStories.title: KMI's Steps 8–10, and its wait recorded honestly
acceptanceCriteria: Steps 8–10 are re-run and count (i) gets a verdict. This is KMI's own work and is independent of KCB.

KMI's status moves ONLY if count (i) is clean AND KCB's media-transform re-run is clean — the ladder says the prose half 'is blocked only because the same scenario also gates KCB's manifest change', and additionally needs `kcs:media-transform` (F4). Record all three conditions and which hold.

userStories.title: What remains after clean re-runs is written down, not left to be rediscovered
acceptanceCriteria: DR-12 and DR-13 (no KCS encoding for §4.2 and §4.3), DR-7 (count (ii)'s encoding must be extended past the fold it predates), W3 (ADR-0013's second-independent-implementation condition on §4.3) and ADR-0014's queued clause change are each recorded in `promotability.md` with an owner named or explicitly unowned.

AG-1 and AG-2 are recorded against the reference implementation: the standalone manifest 0.5.0 removed is still its only crawl path, and its manifest type carries neither `version` nor `schema_id`, so §7 is unexercised outside this tree. These are downstream facts, stated here, not fixed here.

KCB is NOT promoted by this tasklist even on four clean re-runs, and the record says which of the remaining conditions blocks it. The ladder's whole purpose is that a reader should not have to run the audit six times.
`promotability.md`'s 'Cheapest first' ranking is re-ordered to match what these walks changed.
